paragraphs: A Salmonella outbreak linked to broccoli sprouts is now over, according to the CDC [1]. The outbreak affected 34 people across 6 states, resulting in 3 hospitalizations and no deaths [1]. The CDC and FDA determined that the sprouts were grown from a contaminated seed lot imported from New Zealand [18].

Consumers should check their kitchens for Brad's Crunchy Kale & Veggie Chips due to potential thallium contamination [4]. The recall includes Brad's Plant Based Crunchy Kale (2 oz) and Brad's Veggie Chips Kale (3 oz) products [4].

The USDA is issuing a public health alert for Betterballen Foods LLC Bami Rolls sold in Georgia and South Carolina [2]. The frozen 6-piece packages with "BEST BY" dates of October 2027 and lot codes BR-2026-01 and BR-2026-02 contain undeclared sesame allergen [2][11]. Consumers with these products should not eat them [11].

An E. coli O157:H7 outbreak investigation linked to Brookshire Farms pumpkin patch in San Luis Obispo County, California is being wrapped up by local health officials [7]. The outbreak included 15 people, with 5 laboratory-confirmed cases [7].
